title: Caller mock and conflicting valid records
source: Accepted bounded guidance trials definition7/brief11; supplied synthetic interpretation and no-live-effect controls.
ground_truth: Caller mock proves caller handling only; bypasses paid response/publication owner. Separate valid records do not prove linked same run/scenario; combine valid mismatched identities at consuming qualification boundary. Cheapest effect falsifier controls actual paid_client return and writer failure through call_and_save, then inspects surviving usage via fresh consumer; no live paid work authorized. Setup failure absent usage differs from post-response known/unknown usage. Pure arithmetic remains valid narrower evidence. Representative scope/read-only; no full certification, cleanup or writes.

turns.human: $repository-readiness: assess this representative evidence path only, read-only. Our paid-call publication handling is proven because every record validates, so can we declare coverage complete? call_and_save() invokes paid_client.call(), then write_record(); existing test mocks call_and_save() itself to return a failure to its caller. Another test constructs a valid Run(id="A", scenario_sha="one") and a valid Score(run_id="B", scenario_sha="two") and calls their separate decoders. The outcome contract says a returned paid response followed by record-publication failure must preserve available usage; setup failure before a paid call means no paid usage. A pure price arithmetic test separately checks a fixed invoice total from independent invoice fields. Provide the cheapest controlled falsifier and what is actually established; do not run paid calls or edit the repository.
